name: Necrarchs, the Soul Stealers
source: Letters of the Damned #1, Grade 2a warband, converted from mordheimer.net (/docs/warbands/grade-2a-warbands/necrarchs-the-soul-stealers) on 2026-10-10.

heroSlots.notes: Weapons/Armour: A Necrarch Vampire may be armed from the Necrarch Hero Equipment list.

specialRules.name: Leader
specialRules.description: Any models in the warband within 6 inches of the Necrarch Vampire may use his Leadership instead of their own.

specialRules.name: Cause Fear
specialRules.description: Vampires are terrifying Undead creatures and thus cause Fear.

specialRules.name: Wizard
specialRules.description: Necrarch Vampires have one spell randomly generated from the Necromancy spell list.

specialRules.name: Immune to Psychology
specialRules.description: Vampires are not affected by psychology (such as fear) and never leave combat.

specialRules.name: Immune to Poison
specialRules.description: Vampires are not affected by any poison.

specialRules.name: No Pain
specialRules.description: Vampires treat a Stunned result on the Injury chart as Knocked Down.

heroSlots.notes: Weapons/Armour: Acolytes may equip themselves with weapons and armour from the Henchmen equipment list.

specialRules.name: Vassal
specialRules.description: The Acolyte has given himself over to his dark lord. At a whim, the Necrarch can see what the Acolyte sees, hear what he hears, and even speak through his slave. As long as the Necrarch has line of sight to an Acolyte, and the Acolyte is not engaged in hand-to-hand combat, he may use it as a casting point for a spell. Upon a critical failure of a casting (rolling double 1's) regardless of skills such as Mind Focus or the like, the Acolyte must roll on the Injury table and add +1.

henchmenTypes.notes: Weapons/Armour: Skeletal warriors may be equipped with weapons and armour chosen from the Henchmen Equipment list.

specialRules.name: Cause Fear
specialRules.description: Skeletal Warriors are terrifying Undead creatures and therefore cause Fear.

specialRules.name: May not Run
specialRules.description: Skeletal Warriors are slow Undead creatures and may not run (but may charge normally).

specialRules.name: Immune to Psychology
specialRules.description: Skeletal Warriors are not affected by psychology.

specialRules.name: Immune to Poison
specialRules.description: Skeletal Warriors are immune to poisons.

specialRules.name: No Pain
specialRules.description: Skeletal Warriors treat Stunned results as Knocked Down.

specialRules.name: No Brain
specialRules.description: Skeletal Warriors do not gain experience.

henchmenTypes.notes: Weapons/Armour: Abominations do not employ weapons, and suffer no penalties for doing so.

specialRules.name: Cause Fear
specialRules.description: Abominations are terrifying Undead creatures and thus cause Fear.

specialRules.name: Immune to Psychology
specialRules.description: Abominations are not affected by psychology.

specialRules.name: Immune to Poison
specialRules.description: Abominations are immune to poisons.

specialRules.name: Large Target
specialRules.description: Abominations are Large Targets as defined in the shooting rules.

specialRules.name: Powered
specialRules.description: A Necrarch has placed a shard of wyrdstone in the Abomination to bring it life. Should the Abomination be removed from combat, the model who took it down receives a shard of wyrdstone. A new shard is then needed to re-animate the Abomination.

specialRules.name: Spare Parts
specialRules.description: Thanks to the dark magics of their lords and the manner of their construction, Abominations ignore rolls of 1&2 on the post battle Injury Table; they cannot be destroyed.

henchmenTypes.notes: Weapons/Armour: A Waif may be armed with weapons and armour chosen from the Henchmen Equipment list.

exclusiveEquipment.name: Staff of Damnation
exclusiveEquipment.rulesText: Strength As user. Two-Handed: As the Staff of Damnation requires two hands to wield, a model equipped with it may not use a shield, buckler or secondary weapon in close combat. If the model has a shield it will still get a +1 bonus to its armour save against shooting. Magic-well: A Necrarch Vampire may cast a spell into the Staff of Damnation during his Magic phase instead of casting as normal. Upon a successful casting, the spell is stored within the staff. The spell may be released during a later shooting phase in lieu of casting another spell.

exclusiveEquipment.name: Damned Book
exclusiveEquipment.rulesText: Cursed Aura: A model bearing the Damned Book causes all enemy models within 2 inches to suffer a -1 penalty to hit in close combat.

specialRules: Death of the Leader: Should the Necrarch perish, the Thrall shall pick up the mantle of Leader and all conferred bonuses shall be transferred to him. He may immediately roll on the spell list for one spell. You cannot hire another Necrarch, but you may create another Thrall from your current list of Acolyte Heroes. They will retain their current stat-line, but shall gain the benefits of being undead: Immune to Poison & Psychology, causes Fear & suffers No Pain. Should both Necrarch and Thrall be destroyed at once, the evil magics that bind the warband together fade, and all turns to dust.
background: With the destruction of Lahmia the kingdom of Vampires came to an end and the Great Library was burned to the ground. The accumulated knowledge of the ancient Nehekhara was destroyed and many of the disciples of W'soran died in the flames, reluctant to abandon their work. Unfortunately for the world, a handful of Necrarchs fled and survived the pursuit of the armies of the kings of Numas and Zandri, taking with them books, scrolls and other fragments of the dark lore that Nagash had created. They scattered all over the world and hid themselves to patiently wait for the death of their enemies and continue their studies. They built tall towers from where they could study the stars and defend themselves if attacked. News has since spread to these remote strongholds and hidden alcoves of the events occurring in Mordheim, a city ripe for the taking. With the dead calling them forth, the archmages of the Vampire line descend with their minions upon the cursed city to claim its riches, from both those who are dead and those that soon shall be..
